EXAMPLE — FICTIONAL — NOT CUI. Harborline Example Systems LLC (a fictional organisation) System Security Plan excerpt for the Lanternwick Ledger (a fictional system), FedRAMP Moderate. Canary OWNFILE-CANARY-3f9c7a1e.
Section 5.2 AC-2 Account Management. The Lanternwick Ledger ISSO identifies and selects account types (individual, service, and emergency). Account managers are assigned for each account type. Group and role membership conditions are documented in the Access Control Procedure. Accounts are created, enabled, modified, disabled, and removed through the ticketing workflow, and account use is monitored continuously. The ISSO reviews all accounts quarterly; the most recent review completed 2026-08-14.
Section 5.3 AC-17 Remote Access. Remote access to the Lanternwick Ledger is permitted only through the bastion service over TLS 1.3 with FIPS 140-3 validated modules, and every remote session is logged and monitored.
Section 7.1 AU-2 Event Logging. The organisation identifies the events the system is capable of logging — successful and unsuccessful logons, privileged function use, account changes, and configuration changes — and coordinates the logging function with the Harborline security operations team. Logged events are reviewed and updated annually; the last review completed 2026-06-30.
Section 8.4 IA-2 Identification and Authentication. Every organisational user of the Lanternwick Ledger is uniquely identified and authenticated. Multi-factor authentication using WebAuthn/FIDO2 authenticators is enforced for privileged and non-privileged accounts, for local and network access.
Section 9.2 RA-5 Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning. The Lanternwick Ledger is scanned monthly with an authenticated scanner; the most recent scan completed 2026-09-20. Vulnerabilities are remediated within 30 days for high, 90 days for moderate, and 180 days for low, and findings are shared with the ISSO and the system owner.
Section 11.3 SC-13 Cryptographic Protection. Data in transit uses TLS 1.3 and data at rest uses AES-256, both through FIPS 140-3 validated modules.
Section 12.1 IR-4 Incident Handling. The Harborline Incident Response Plan covers preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication, and recovery; lessons learned are incorporated into procedures after every incident.
